DISCOVER ST NICHOLAS' SCHOOL
St Nicholas’ School is an exceptional independent day school for girls aged 3–16 and boys aged 3–7 years.
Founded in 1935, we are defined by our strong community spirit and unwavering commitment to educational excellence. We provide a nurturing environment where every pupil is empowered to thrive — celebrating individuality, encouraging personal growth, and inspiring each child to realise their full potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior School Pastoral Care | St Nicholas' School, Hampshire
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care in Seniors
FOCUSING ON THE INDIVIDUAL
As girls enter the Seniors, our aim is to ensure a smooth transition for all girls, regardless of whether they join from our Juniors or another school. We are keen to help girls develop, both academically and personally, and the pastoral system is very much designed with the individual girl in mind.
Pastoral care in the Senior School is about placing the individual at the centre of our community. Our experienced team gets to know the girls, their strengths and challenges, to give each girl the personalised support that will allow them to develop at their own pace and time. We create an environment where our pupils are able to flourish. Not only do we encourage them to seek support or advice when they need it, but we also empower them to problem solve and empathise with others, developing the skills they require to become balanced, compassionate and resilient young women.
TUTORS
Our dedicated team of tutors is at the heart of this system. Our tutors take the time to get to know the girls both in school and through a range of enrichment activities such as camp outs, fun trips and residentials. The girls will see their tutors three times a day, allowing for regular check-ins and opportunities for any concerns or questions to be raised.
The tutors are also the first port of call for any parent queries, allowing us to work as a team, supporting the pupil whilst encouraging independence and developing confidence. Most lessons in lower seniors will be taught in tutor group, whilst around 40% of lessons are taught with other members of the year group. This allows the girls to develop friendships with a range of people, and creates a greater sense of community within the year group.
As well as a tutor, each Year 7 is also given a 'Big Sister’. This is an older pupil who will meet with them regularly, getting to know them better and supporting them wherever possible. The Big Sister acts as a sounding board as well as being that more personal ‘friendly face’ if they have worries or concerns.
COMMUNITY
Our pupils want to contribute to society and know they have something to give. All staff members share the responsibility of caring for our pupils and we encourage a culture of approachability throughout the school. This ethos also underpins the relationship we create with parents. We know that providing for the well-being of our pupils is central in helping them to become purposeful, caring and happy individuals.
Each girl is a member of a House, which runs vertically from Year 2 through to Year 11. Regular house competitions allow the girls to get to know those in other year groups, as well as creating a sense of community. The coveted House Cup is awarded each year at prize giving for the house that has collected the most House Points throughout the year. The girls can work towards taking on a Leadership role in the Houses in Year 11. The houses also run regular fundraising initiatives for a range of charities of their choosing.
EXTRA SUPPORT
At times we all need a helping hand, and we know teenage years can be difficult. Our Heads of Phase oversee the tutor system and are poised to step in when needed.
One-to-one support can be given through mentoring, or more specialist guidance can be offered through our highly skilled team of ELSA’s (Emotional Literacy Support Assistance), Active Listeners or through the School Counsellor.
Jasper our school dog is also on hand for those days when we just need a hug!
"We feel very informed and impressed at the clear expertise of all subject teachers and their dedication. The teaching and pastoral team have enabled our daughter to flourish and we feel very lucky that she is at St Nicks." Senior School Parent

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts | St Nicholas' School, Hampshire
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts
PASSION AND INCLUSION
Performing Arts at St Nicholas’ School forms a varied and exciting part of our broad curriculum, in which all pupils from Nursery to Seniors are encouraged to explore and participate.
Alongside trips, workshops and a host of co-curricular clubs, pupils can take part in our inclusive school productions, developing the confidence that comes with performing in front of an audience for the budding actors and dancers, and learning new skills for those who are more interested in the technical and backstage aspects.
At St Nicholas’ School the Performing Arts Department collaborates closely with the Music Department on school musical performances and benefits enormously from our exceptional Performing Arts Centre, The Pritchard Hall, with adaptable proscenium arch stage, professional-level technical equipment and excellent views of the stage provided from the raked seating on the lower and upper floors. Our excellent theatre space is also used by professional visiting theatre companies, giving our pupils a true insight into the theatre industry.
PERFORMING ARTS IN NURSERY AND INFANTS
Whilst learning to express themselves both individually and in groups within their weekly Performing Arts lessons, our Nursery and Infant pupils have many opportunities to develop and demonstrate their skills in assemblies, Nativity plays, and a summer concert performed in the Pritchard Hall.
"We wanted to say how much we loved the St Nick's School of Rock production. We enjoyed every minute, and were in awe of the brilliance of the cast. Please pass on our heartfelt congratulations to all concerned." St Nicholas' School Parents
We are delighted to celebrate the incredible achievements of Tilly in Year 5, whose dedication and passion for dance have led to success on both national and international stages.
Huge congratulations to two of our Junior School pupils (Year 6 and Year 4), who enjoyed a fantastic trip to Birmingham last weekend to take part in the MTI (Music Theatre International) Junior Theatre Festival.
We are incredibly proud to share that Francesca and Sophie in Year 6 recently enjoyed an unforgettable opportunity to perform on a professional stage alongside the West End Tenors.
Today was filled with reflection and nonstop talk about our Senior Production… and for good reason! Last Friday and Saturday night, our Senior girls lit up the stage with a high‑energy, show‑stopping performance of Footloose.
“We loved The Sound of Music performance last night and were so impressed with the girls - excellent singing, not a single word or line forgotten and super acting - your drama team should be so proud of such an exceptional achievement." St Nicholas' School Parent

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior Curriculum | St Nicholas' School, Hampshire
pageCache.text:
Senior Curriculum
ENCOURAGING ACADEMIC SUCCESS
At St Nicholas’ School we believe that every girl should be given the opportunity to excel across a full range of subjects, whatever her ability.
Our GCSE results are excellent, ranking amongst the best nationally, and our alumni build on this solid foundation to achieve further success in their chosen pathways. Small class sizes at St Nicholas' School allow our teachers to focus on teaching and learning, providing individual attention to meet the specific needs of each pupil.
At St Nicholas’ School, we are proud of our girls' strong record of achieving success in all areas. We strongly believe that academic success is embedded within a positive attitude towards learning, reflecting our core values that are incorporated within the curriculum and referred to as THRIVE.
Our senior curriculum is constantly evolving to ensure variety and incremental growth.
Art Each year, pupils dive into an exciting exploration of drawing, painting, printmaking, photography, and 3D skills. They’ll craft their own unique sketchbooks, capturing personal ideas and documenting their creative adventures step by step.
Textiles Pupils embark on a journey to master a variety of techniques, including stitching, sewing machine skills, machine felting, advanced embroidery, couching, reverse applique, and 3D modelling. Through exciting activities like educational trips, the exploration of inspiring artists and designers, and the integration of photography and drawing into their textile projects, pupils will cultivate a dynamic range of design and making skills.
Classic Civilisation We all know history repeats itself. Our pupils learn about the past (Greeks and Romans) which aids them in understanding our present time. They also explore the exciting world of Mythology!
Latin Studying the Latin language reinforces a knowledge of English and MFL languages and improves vocabulary. From the Romans we have learnt traditions that are still in use today, like wearing the wedding ring on the third finger of the left hand. Learning Latin helps pupils to make connections and step out of their comfort zones!
Pupils gain essential digital skills for the modern world, including the basics of coding and creating their own programs whilst solving problems. With a strong foundation in digital literacy and coding, our pupils are well-prepared for future opportunities in a technology-driven world.
English is the subject that underpins all the rest! Therefore, our lessons are spent developing our pupils’ communication skills of reading, writing, and speaking and listening, through the study of literary rich texts and imaginative tasks from across the genres and ages.
We ensure that Food as a subject is so much more than just cooking. We introduce our pupils to important knowledge of food hygiene, key knife skills and of course understanding the importance of the food groups and how they interact with our body. We do all this while still cooking some delicious foods to bring home to share!
Understanding the world around us has never been more important and in Geography we aim to bring this knowledge alive. Through a diverse range of topics, from learning about our UK home to the issues faced by populations around the world, pupils build up a better understanding of our world. Fieldtrips, such as the Hayling Island coasts trip helps to bring the concepts to life.
History is an exciting and diverse subject. We aim to inspire pupils’ curiosity to know more about the past and to equip pupils to ask perceptive questions, think critically, weigh evidence, sift arguments and develop perspective and judgement. History helps pupils to understand the complexity of people’s lives, the process of change, the diversity of societies and relationships between different groups, as well as their own identity and the challenges of their time.
We aim to inspire, engage and challenge pupils during their learning, regardless of ability. The curriculum is relevant and links with careers and other subjects. Opportunities are provided for pupils to participate in Maths competitions, problem-solving and other enrichment activities. In recent years we have had a large increase in the number of pupils who go on and study Mathematics at a higher level.
French Salut! We encourage our pupils to enjoy speaking French through listening to pop songs, playing fun games and preparing dialogues, whilst always developing their range of vocabulary to talk about everyday life, family and friends, interests and opinions. Pupils develop their communication skills as well as knowledge of the French culture. All pupils are offered the opportunity to go to Normandy, France, when in Year 7, for a week of total immersion and fun!
Mandarin Learning Mandarin, the most spoken language in the world, helps our pupils learn more about China’s charming culture and ancient history through this fascinating language. In our lessons we learn a range of topics, where pupils get to experience writing Chinese characters and speaking the language using the four different tones.
Spanish ¡Hola! Pupils explore Spanish culture and the Spanish language through research, games and quizzes. Pupils begin to discover how to communicate in Spanish and learn how to pronounce words, introduce themselves, talk about family life and how to travel around town.
Music lessons are fun, inclusive and creative. Pupils learn about musical styles from around the world, expanding their knowledge of different musical genres, including developing an understanding of Music Technology using Apple Mac computers and working collaboratively to compose and perform their own music. All pupils will have the opportunity to perform during the school year, whether as part of an ensemble or as a soloist.
Dance and Drama are used to create scripted and devised work. Pupils work through a range of genres from pantomime to Shakespeare and physical theatre. The enjoyment of class performance rolls over into the Senior production where pupils can take part in performing on stage, being part of the backstage crew or controlling the technical elements of the performance.
We aim to embed a life-long love for physical activity in all our senior pupils. Girls benefit from working in small, streamed teaching groups with specialist staff and top-quality equipment. There is a strong emphasis not only on refining and developing individual skills but also on teamwork. The girls are taught to use a variety of strategies when faced with competition. There is also an increasing emphasis on leadership. The curriculum is enriched by an extensive co-curricular programme where every girl, regardless of ability, can enjoy being physically active and challenged through a variety of sports and activities.
The teaching of Religious Studies at St Nicholas’ School provides our pupils with spiritual, moral, social and cultural development. Pupils are encouraged to consider their own values, beliefs and ideas, as well as those of others. They study the history, beliefs, worship, festivals and lifestyle of different world religions. Discussion and questioning are promoted in lessons to develop spiritual growth, reflection and self-expression.
From Year 7, all pupils study the three sciences separately. The curriculum is designed to build on the knowledge gained at KS2 and to encourage independent thinking. The course broadly follows the National Curriculum but, in many cases, the work is taken to a higher level. In addition, pupils develop their ability to plan, carry out and evaluate their own experiments. They develop their maths skills, literacy skills and enquiry processes.
Biology Pupils learn about the Science of Life. Everything from cells, organ systems, the basics of genetics to ecology. They find out how every living thing is dependent on another for its survival.
Chemistry Have you ever wondered what everything is made of? Our pupils have the opportunity to carry out a variety of different chemical reactions while learning about elements, compounds and mixtures.
Physics Studying Physics helps our pupils find a key to the Universe. They start to see how different things are connected, answering the bigger questions about our planet and beyond. The study of Physics helps with key skills such as problem-solving, logic and reasoning.
"A huge thanks to the Year 10 teaching team. We feel very informed and impressed at the clear expertise of all subject teachers and their dedication. Over the last few years the teaching and pastoral team have enabled our daughter to flourish and we feel very lucky that she is where she is at St Nicks." Senior School Parent

SUPPORTING LEARNING IN SENIORS
At St Nicholas' we offer all our Senior pupils drop-in clinics providing clarification or support regarding a particular topic or unit of work should they require it.
These sessions provide pupils with the opportunity to receive individual attention to address any issues or problem areas that they may have encountered during lessons and for our GCSE pupils to receive further support and guidance on examination technique and problem-solving scenarios.
Curriculum Support at St Nicholas’ School is designed to give our pupils a boost in their learning and covers a spectrum of needs, from support within the curriculum to helping those with individual learning difficulties or where English is their second language.
The teaching provides support with literacy, language, comprehension, mathematics, study skills and exam skills. Sessions are designed to meet the pupil’s specific needs, help them to enjoy learning and to develop a range of strategies to become independent learners. This support is provided by trained staff to meet a pupil's individual needs. Pupils may be tutored in small groups, or they may be given additional help within a lesson.
Our Curriculum Support staff liaise with subject teachers to ensure that pupils receive the support they need in class. Small classes enable subject teachers to provide pupils with additional help and scaffolding for their learning.
2025 GCSE RESULTS
100% grades 9-4 (A*-C) in: Art, Biology, Business Studies, Chemistry, Classical Civilisation, Computer Science, Drama, English Language, English Literature, French, Food Preparation and Nutrition, Geography, History, Mandarin, Music, Physics and Spanish.
46% of pupils achieved top grades 9-7 (A*/A).
38% of pupils earned 11 GCSEs — compared to the national average of just 1.6%.
50% of all Year 10 Statistics grades were 9-7 (A*/A).
OUR 3-WAY PARTNERSHIP WITH YOU
We believe in fostering a strong child-parent-school partnership.
Through parent evenings, coffee mornings and our Super Curriculum, we share regular updates, current topics and themes, books we are reading, learning techniques and 'next steps' to support and educate our parents in their child's learning journey.

Pupils at St Nicholas' School THRIVE through Togetherness, Hard Work, Resilience, Independence, Valuing Others and Excellence
Our core values are reflected through THRIVE, strengthening the ethical aspects of our subjects and encouraging our pupils to think critically about their actions and decisions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision and Values | St Nicholas’ School, Hampshire
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
EDUCATIONAL AIMS AND ETHOS
St Nicholas' School is a happy, thriving school where education is seen as a partnership between teachers, pupils and parents. We are proud to play our part in the development of children from their earliest years through to sixteen.
We have three major educational aims:
All of our pupils have the opportunities to fulfil their abilities; many going on to be leaders in the fields of academia, industry, business and the arts. Whatever they become, we believe the school plays a vital role in helping them to recognise their strengths and realise their goals.
We aim to instil them with a sense of pride in everything they do, and the vision to see the virtue in the endeavours of others.
CORE VALUES
At St Nicholas’ School, our educational philosophy is embodied in THRIVE — an acronym representing the core values that form the heart of our school community. These principles create a positive, supportive environment where every pupil can flourish.
At St Nicholas' School, pupils will THRIVE through:
THRIVE is woven into both our curriculum and co-curricular programmes, strengthening the ethical focus of learning across all subjects. It encourages pupils to think deeply about their choices and actions while providing a consistent framework for personal growth and contribution to the community.

Nursery Curriculum
BUILDING FIRM FOUNDATIONS
Our unique teaching methods combine creative play with engaging lessons and activities, whilst focusing on building strong foundations in development and learning.
Our Nursery curriculum is based on the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS Areas of Learning and Development) and we personalise our teaching and learning approach to cater to children's individual needs, encouraging growth, supporting in areas of challenge, and empowering them to reach their full potential.
Every child is unique and there are a number of characteristics that show the different ways in which children actively engage and learn, playing a central role in their learning, and in becoming an effective learner. These Characteristics of Effective Learning run through and underpin all seven Areas of Learning and Development within the EYFS.

Playing and exploring - Engagement
Active Learning - Motivation
Creative and Critical Thinking - Thinking

Register Online
START YOUR JOURNEY
To apply for a place at St Nicholas' School, please complete the registration form below.
This form takes around 10 minutes to complete. When completing the personal details for parents, please include the details of both parents. Ahead of starting, have ready a scan of your child’s passport photo page, birth certificate and if applicable, copies of any recent school reports and/or educational assessment reports as these will need to be uploaded at the end of the form.
Once your completed form has been received, along with a non-refundable registration fee of £120 (per child), our Admissions Team will be in touch to guide you through the next stages of the admissions process.

Music
EXPRESSION AND PERFORMANCE
St Nicholas’ School has a reputation for its excellent music provision where every pupil is encouraged to explore and fulfil their musical potential through an array of co-curricular activities, performance opportunities and ensemble experiences.
Pupils across the school, from Nursery to Seniors, participate in an extensive range of ensembles, enhancing their musical development. Making music with others, such as belonging to a choir, an orchestra or a band, is vital to hone their skills and is an excellent way of making friends and working as a team.
Alongside our ensembles, over 160 music lessons are taught each week by a team of visiting peripatetic teachers. Currently, over 60% of all students receive lessons on at least one instrument. The combination of specialist teaching across a wide range of instruments and excellent resources, provides our pupils with a supportive and inspiring environment in which to flourish to a very high standard.
St Nicholas’ School pupils benefit from all musical performances taking place in the Pritchard Hall, our purpose-built Performing Arts Theatre with raked seating on the lower and upper floors and an orchestra pit, as well as further co-curricular experiences such as music trips, opportunities to watch a variety of concerts and the chance to perform in the wider community.
MUSIC IN NURSERY AND INFANTS
Our Nursery and Infant School pupils are taught music weekly by specialist staff. Alongside this, pupils take part in weekly singing assemblies and can join the Infant Choir. There are regular opportunities for pupils to perform together during the year within assemblies, plays and a special summer concert in the Pritchard Hall.
All our pupils in Years 1 and 2 receive group violin lessons with Year 2 pupils having the option of individual violin and piano lessons.
Year 6 pupil Violet has achieved outstanding success at the Aldershot and Farnborough Music Festival, hosted by Salesian College Farnborough, earning a Distinction for her impressive and confident performance.
Following a successful Easter course at the Royal Academy of Music, Theodora has been awarded a place at its prestigious Primary Academy — a wonderful recognition of her dedication and musical talent.
Our annual Senior Music Evening saw girls from Years 7–11 deliver an outstanding concert, showcasing exceptional musicianship, creativity and passion across a wide range of musical styles.
On the first day of the Christmas holidays, a group of our Junior and Senior School string musicians visited Hill House Nursing Home to perform a medley of festive music, continuing our much-loved annual tradition.
"A quick note to say congratulations and thank you to yourself and the music teachers for a lovely Informal Concert last night! You really enabled the girls to shine with some stunning accompaniment arrangements and I felt that the broad variety of pieces performed indicated that each girl had a connection with their chosen piece. Bravo and thank you to all you and your team do." St Nicholas' School Parent

Lunch Menus
All pupils enjoy delicious hot and cold lunches in our Dining Hall. Meals are freshly prepared and cooked daily on-site by our catering company Lodestone House and rotated on a three-week basis.
Meals are designed to provide a well-balanced diet which is both nutritional and enjoyable, and include fruit and vegetables to encourage healthy eating.
Pupils can choose food from the hot main meal bar (both meat and vegetarian options), salad bar or deli bar and also have the choice of a hot dessert or something from the dessert fridge.
A selection of freshly baked bread and homemade soup is also available every day and all dietary requirements are catered for.

St Nicholas' School PTA
A THRIVING SCHOOL COMMUNITY
Our Parent and Teacher Association (PTA) plays a vital role in bringing our school community together, raising funds to support local charities, school initiatives and enhancing our pupils' school experience.
With sustainability at the heart of everything they do, our dedicated PTA organises a range of successful fundraising events including the popular sell-out Fireworks Night, exciting Discos, fun-filled Pizza and Movie Nights and the annual always-anticipated Parent Quiz Night.
We invite all parents to get involved with the PTA - whether you can spare a lot of time or just a little, your help is always appreciated. The team is friendly and welcoming, and it is a great way to connect with other parents and become more engaged in school life.
If you are interested in learning more or joining in, please email the PTA at st-nicholas-pta@outlook.com or come along to one of our upcoming events.
Our Nursery, Infant and Junior pupils enjoyed an egg-cellent Easter Treasure Hunt this morning, complete with a visit from the Easter Bunny, creative craft activities and fantastic support from our Year 11 helpers.
What a fantastic evening we had at our annual Parents and Teachers Quiz Night last Friday! The hall was filled with laughter, friendly rivalry, and plenty of brain‑teasing challenges as our school community came together.
Last Friday evening, the sun was shining and the atmosphere was electric as the St Nicholas’ PTA hosted their first-ever school festival – and what an unforgettable night it was.
Staff and pupils have had a lot of fun trying to 'Guess the Eggs' with a variety of strategies and problem solving techniques on display! Can you guess how many there are?

pageCache.pageTitle: More Able and Talented | St Nicholas' School
pageCache.text:
More Able and Talented
At St Nicholas' School, we aim to nurture, develop and stretch our pupils’ talents and interests. We are committed to providing a challenging and dynamic curriculum, which provides opportunity and supports our More Able and Talented (MAT) learners.
All our pupils are challenged at their level through differentiated activities that extend their learning and curiosity. Lessons are differentiated appropriately, providing challenge and pace.
Teachers provide open-ended tasks that encourage critical thinking, problem solving and creativity. For example, more complex puzzles, deeper exploration of a topic, advanced language and literacy opportunities, such as extended storytelling or writing, help stretch pupils’ abilities.
In addition, teachers support all children by consistently fostering independence, encouraging them to take risks in their learning and asking though-provoking questions that require deeper reflection.
Opportunities with peer collaboration with similarly able children and personalised learning journeys also contribute to ensuring that all children are challenged and remain engaged according to their ability.
We endeavour to provide a stimulating experience for all our pupils, both inside and outside of the classroom, through co-curricular clubs and societies, enrichment activities, workshops and trips, visits by outside speakers, and competitions to aid in enriching their learning.
"We are super proud of our daughter but also absolutely recognise the encouragement and support she had from her teachers at St Nicholas' in really helping her to achieve strong GCSE results. Her ambition and determination now are so very much down to the support she had at that time. Thank you and your academic team again and wishing you all the best for the future academic years."
We are delighted to recognise alumni Aimee’s exceptional contribution to college sport, highlighted by her outstanding achievements and dedication in both netball and basketball over the past two years.
We are delighted to celebrate the incredible achievements of Tilly in Year 5, whose dedication and passion for dance have led to success on both national and international stages.
There was a wonderful buzz of excitement this afternoon as our Year 7 pupils gathered to take part in the school’s Spelling Bee competition, bringing energy, enthusiasm and a real sense of friendly competition to the event.
Issy (Year 6) proudly represented Hampshire County at the British Judo Association Southern Area competition, where she demonstrated outstanding skill, determination and sportsmanship.
